subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/429s and timeouts impacting NimbusHealth - request for exec attention
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: NimbusHealth SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: High 5xx/429s + timeouts across inference endpoints — immediate help needed

Hi Vanessa,

We just experienced a multi-hour outage window this morning where our patient-facing summarization calls started returning 5xx and 429s intermittently, and a lot of requests timed out then retried from our side which compounded the load. This hit our production traffic from 08:10–10:40 PST and caused visible errors in the UI.

We escalated to your support but wanted to loop you directly — we need transparency on root cause, mitigation plan, and immediate capacity or config changes to avoid recurrence. Our SREs see elevated retry loops originating from client SDK behavior and some backend 504s/502s. Attaching a short timeline.

Can we get an executive brief and commitments on the next steps? This is impacting our care workflows for a small subset of clinics.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Product, NimbusHealth
Attachment: incident_timeline.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: NimbusHealth SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Triage notes — increased 429s tied to retry amplification + cache miss patterns

Quick triage summary (initial):
- Window: 08:06–10:42 PST
- Observation 1: A subset (~18%) of client requests had long tail latencies (p95 -> 3.1s, max 18s) leading to SDK retries that did not honor exponential backoff (client-side config).
- Observation 2: Several worker pools hit concurrent request saturation due to KV cache misses after a rolling redeploy; cold-cache token expansion increased per-request compute.
- Observation 3: Some requests routed to v2 quantized model variant which had higher CPU contention on the node type; combined with the retry storm this caused queue growth and 502/504 upstream timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:20–10:40):
- Deployed routing override: prefer v1 stable variant for Nimbus production routes.
- Increased per-customer reserved capacity by 20% (burst) for 2 hours.
- Applied temporary stricter ingress rate-limiter at the edge for noisy SDKs.

Next steps: full timeline export, SLO delta analysis, and a follow-up runbook update. Will push a hotfix to prevent non-idempotent retry amplification next release.

-Jonas
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo_delta_matrix.csv (CSV)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 13:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec summary (interim) + customer comms plan

Elena — thanks for your patience. Short executive summary for your leadership and internal comms: 

What happened (interim):
- A combination of rolling redeploy (cache churn) + client-side retry patterns created a retry storm that amplified traffic and exposed a capacity edge case for a quantized model variant. This produced transient 5xx/429 errors and user-visible timeouts between 08:06–10:42 PST.

What we did (immediate):
- Routing override to stable model variant; temporary capacity bump + edge ingress rate limiting; SDK guidance to limit retry aggressiveness.

Commitments (what you'll see from us):
- Within 24h: detailed RCA and timeline (including logs and request traces).
- Within 72h: a runbook update and a mitigation patch to reduce retry amplification risk.
- Within 2 weeks: SLO tuning recommendation and a proposed capacity reservation change (if accepted) to prevent recurrence.

I will be your single point of contact for status updates; we'll provide a concise exec brief ready for your leadership meeting this afternoon.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sre_playbook_v1.2.docx (Word, 6 pages)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident analysis — RCA and proposed mitigations

Team — following deeper analysis, consolidated RCA and action items: 

Root causes:
1) Cache churn during rolling deploys increased model startup/kv expansion latency for a subset of routes (observed on nodes with cold KV footprint).
2) Default client SDK retry policy (3 fast retries, no jitter/backoff tuning) amplified the transient latency into a traffic surge.
3) Routing policy allowed non-homogeneous model variants with different resource profiles for the same route; no automatic fallback prioritization existed.

Immediate fixes implemented:
- Routing policy override to stable variant (rolled back after stabilizing).
- Per-account emergency reserve capacity + temporary ingress throttling.
- Client guidance sent to Nimbus SRE to adjust SDK retry behavior.

Follow-up deliverables (owners + ETA):
- Runbook additions for retry storms and redeploy cache warming (owner: Jonas) — ETA 2026-03-05.
- Alerting gaps: add synthetic SLO probes that measure tail latency and end-to-end error amplification (owner: Sean) — ETA 2026-03-04.
- SLO tuning: produce per-route SLO delta and recommended guardrails (owner: Rishi) — ETA 2026-03-08.
- Product change: routing prioritization by model resource profile + automatic fallback to compatible variant (owner: Eng Platform) — planning meeting 2026-03-02.

I'll prepare a consolidated post-incident note for execs summarizing impact metrics, mitigations, and recommended contractual remedies (credits / SLA exception) for review.

-Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML / Inference Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@nimbushealth.com>, NimbusHealth SRE <sre@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 15:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Final incident note + commitments for NimbusHealth (impact, RCA, actions)

Elena — please find below the executive-friendly summary and our commitments. We appreciate your partnership during the incident.

Impact:
- Window: 2026-02-26 08:06–10:42 PST.
- Error surface: ~2.7% of requests returned 5xx/429; peak p95 latency increased from 0.9s -> 3.1s for affected routes. Estimated customer-facing errors: ~1,400 failed requests.

Root cause (short):
- Cold cache inflation during a rolling deploy combined with aggressive client retries and a routing policy that allowed a higher-contention model variant to receive production traffic.

Commitments and timeline:
- Today: we’ve provided an incident timeline and initial synthetic checks. (completed)
- 2026-03-04: New synthetic tail-latency probes and alerting for amplification (owner: Sean Gallagher).
- 2026-03-05: Runbook updates for redeploy cache warming + retry-storm steps (owner: Jonas Weber).
- 2026-03-08: SLO delta report and recommended guardrails for your routes (owner: Rishi Malhotra).
- 2026-03-15: Routing prioritization feature scoping and proposed rollout plan; if accepted, staged rollout to Nimbus routes.

Compensation / contractual note: we will propose a one-time credit to NimbusHealth for the incident while we finalize SLO deltas and agree on any longer-term reservation changes. Marissa will share a formal note on that separately.

If you want a short call with execs and the SRE leads to walk through the RCA, we can schedule today or tomorrow — please propose a time.

Thanks again, and we will keep you updated at each milestone.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
